newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end off on profit-taking, options.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end off on profit-taking, options.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed down again Friday on the settlement in New York of Telebras options and local profit-taking ahead of the U.S.'s Columbus Day holiday Monday, brokers said.
"The decline had to do with settlement of options on Telebras ADRs," one dealer said, adding investors also sold Brazilian shares ahead of the long weekend in the U.S.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most traded shares slipped 180 points, or 0.27 percent, to end at 66,087 points on turnover of 420 million reais.

The bolsa was higher most of the day, but prices gave way on a rash of selling at session's end spurred by Telebras options settlements in New York and investors dumping positions ahead of the long weekend in the U.S.
Brokers said the market maintained the trendlessness it has shown all week, showing itself volatile ahead of October 16 futures settlements and October 21 options expiry.
"There was no good reason for the market to fall today, " one broker said. "Interest rates are down, the Dow is up and there is absolutely no bad news."
Among blue chips, benchmark Telebras preferred fell 0.74 percent to end at 80.70 reais, while its voting common dipped 0.13 percent to 68.40 reais.
Other leaders also declined. State miner Vale do Rio Doce preferred fell 1.14 percent to close at 20.75 reais and Banco do Brasil dropped 1.51 percent to 9.11 reais.
On the other hand, state oil monopoly Petrobras' preferred rose 1.24 percent at 120.99 reais, while its common share ended 2.05 percent higher at 79.60 reais.

The day's big gainer was Minas Gerais state's Cemig common, which soared 10.3 percent to end at 48.00 reais on rumors that a Chilean company will buy a 33 percent block of common shares in the company. The share surged 9.3 percent on Thursday.
The power blue chip, Eletrobras, ended flat at 317.00 reais after rising all week on good prospects for privatization of Brazil's electrical sector.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) of nine most-liquid power stocks edged up 0.06 percent to end at 1,725 points. -- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
